read.sections.0.text.back: The environment is everything around us: land, water, air, plants and animals. The environment changes over time. As the climate changes, some places now get heavier rain, while other places experience longer dry seasons. People also change places. For example, when many trees are cut down on a hillside, heavy rain can wash away the soil more easily because there are no roots to hold it. In Brookside, heavier rain now sometimes submerges the low footbridge. Children use the bridge to go to school, and traders use it to go to the market. The community needs a plan.
read.sections.0.text.source: The environment is everything around us: land, water, air, plants and animals. Environments change over time. As the climate changes, some places now get heavier rain, while others have longer dry seasons. People change places too. For example, when many trees are cut down on a hillside, heavy rain can wash the soil away more easily, because there are no roots to hold it. In Brookside, heavier rain now sometimes covers the low footbridge. Children use the bridge to reach school, and traders use it to reach the market. The community needs a plan.

read.sections.1.text.note: Translator: 'Great Green Wall' is kept in English as the project's name (it also appears in source 2). Malaysian media sometimes write 'Tembok Hijau Besar'. Check which one to use. Back-translation check: 'Great Green Wall' is kept in English here and in sources.2. Check whether to use 'Tembok Hijau Besar'. Fixed: 'tempat itu' became 'tempat masing-masing' so that each response fits its own place.
read.sections.1.text.back: All over the world, communities adapt to changes in their environment. In Bangladesh, many fields stay under water for months in the rainy season. Some farmers build floating gardens from water plants and grow vegetables on them. In Africa, countries from Senegal to Djibouti are working on the Great Green Wall. They plant trees and look after the land so that the land does not turn into desert. In many coastal areas in Asia, people plant mangrove trees, whose roots help protect the coast from waves. Each one of these is a response that suits that place.
read.sections.1.text.source: Around the world, communities adapt to changes in their environment. In Bangladesh, many fields stay under water for months in the rainy season. Some farmers build floating gardens from water plants and grow vegetables on top. In Africa, countries from Senegal to Djibouti are working on the Great Green Wall. They plant trees and care for the land to stop it from turning into desert. On many coasts in Asia, people plant mangrove trees, whose roots help protect the shore from waves. Each of these is a response that fits the local place.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: Communities around the world adapt. In Bangladesh, many fields are under water in the rainy season. So some farmers make gardens that float. They grow vegetables on them. In Africa, many countries are planting trees in a large dry area. The trees help stop the land from becoming desert. In part of Asia, people plant trees by the sea. Their roots help protect the land from waves. Each response suits its place.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: Communities around the world adapt. In Bangladesh, many fields are under water in the rainy season. So some farmers make gardens that float. They grow vegetables on top. In Africa, many countries plant trees across a wide, dry area. The trees help stop the land from turning into desert. In parts of Asia, people plant trees by the sea. The roots help keep the land safe from waves. Each response fits its place.

read.sections.2.text.back: A response only works if people can use it. Look at the three ideas for Brookside. Warning signboards are quick to make, but they do not make the bridge safer, and some people cannot read them. Raising the bridge reduces the risk, and a ramp helps people who use wheelchairs or push trolleys. Phone warnings can tell people earlier, but not everyone has a phone or data. Printed notices at the market reach more people. Making sure everyone can use a plan is called inclusiveness. Often, two ideas together work better than one, and it is good to ask the people who use the bridge.
read.sections.2.text.source: A response only works if people can use it. Look at the three ideas for Brookside. A warning sign is quick, but it does not make the bridge safer, and some people cannot read it. Raising the bridge lowers the risk, and a ramp helps people who use wheelchairs or push carts. Phone alerts can warn people early, but not everyone has a phone or data. Printed notices at the market reach more people. Making sure that everyone can use a plan is called inclusion. Often, two ideas together work better than one, and it helps to ask the people who use the bridge.

read.sections.2.simpler.back: A plan only works if people can use it. A signboard is quick to make. But it does not make the bridge safe. A higher bridge is safer. A ramp helps people who cannot climb stairs. Phone warnings tell people earlier. But not everyone has a phone. Paper notices at the market also help. When everyone can use a plan, that is called inclusiveness. Two ideas together can work better than one.

Two ideas together can work better than one.

watch.summary.note: Translator: 'Disability' is translated as 'orang kurang upaya' (OKU), the usual Malaysian term. Check that it is right for a child audience. Back-translation check: Check that 'orang kurang upaya' / 'kanak-kanak kurang upaya' is right for a child audience. 'Bukan setiap kanak-kanak' is slightly calqued; 'Tidak semua kanak-kanak' may read more naturally.
watch.summary.back: In this short UNICEF video, people talk about climate change and people with disabilities. Heavy rain, landslides and storms can cause problems for whole towns. But the video says these events are even harder for children with disabilities. Not every child can hear a warning sound. Not every child can run to a safe place. So these children need different plans. The main message is to make these plans together, before danger comes. Ask people with disabilities, because they know what they need. The video asks for warnings that work for all, safe routes for all, and safe places that can be used by all. When you plan for everyone from the start, the plan is better for all.
watch.summary.source: In this short UNICEF video, people talk about climate change and disability. Heavy rain, landslides and storms can cause problems for a whole town. But the video says these events are even harder for children with disabilities. Not every child can hear a warning sound. Not every child can run to a safe place. So these children need different plans. The main message is to make these plans together, before danger comes. Ask people with disabilities, because they know what they need. The video asks for warnings that work for all, a safe path for all, and safe places that all can use. When you plan for everyone from the start, the plan is better for all.
